newsitem.title: USA: ICE HOCKEY-USA HOCKEY NAMES LAMORIELLO GM OF OLYMPIC TEAM.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-USA HOCKEY NAMES LAMORIELLO GM OF OLYMPIC TEAM.

text.p: USA Hockey on Friday named New Jersey Devils executive Lou Lamoriello to be general manager of the team the United States will send to Nagano, Japan for the 1998 Winter Olympics.

Lamoriello, president and general manager of the NHL's New Jersey franchise, held a similar post with the U.S. squad that scored a stunning upset victory in the inaugural World Cup of Hockey in September.

"I have known Lou Lamoriello a long time...," said Walter Bush, president of USA Hockey, the sport's national governing body, in announcing the appointment. "He led the U.S. to our first World Cup win and is the man for the job."
Lamoriello's duties will include the selection of the coaching staff and 23-player roster for the U.S. men's team for what is being billed as the Olympic dream tournament.

For the first time in the Olympics, National Hockey League players will participate in the ice hockey tournament at the 1998 Games. The NHL is expected to supply players to Canada, Russia, Sweden, Finland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Germany as well as the United States, creating a number of dream teams.
"It's an honour and I am flattered with this appointment," said Lamoriello, from Scottsdale, Arizona, where the NHL general managers are holding meetings.
"So far, there is no timetable for the appointment of a coach," Lamoriello said.

"We appreciate what the players who won the World Cup in September did for us, but there is no guarantee the team will be exactly the same. We have a quantity of young American players who are maturing fast and may have be considered."
The NHL is expected to shut down operations for two weeks in February of 1998 while the Olympics take place.
"This is a first time thing," said Lamoriello. "The NHL is still working on release dates for the players who will be picked."
